text:
Marta: pushed INT8-KV to canary-3 for the 13B runtime this morning. memory for KV down ~22% but seeing decode-quality drift on our smoke eval set. attaching quick profile below. :eyes:

Raj: can you paste the profiling snippet? also which calibration did you use? per-tensor or per-channel?

Marta: per-tensor, because it was faster. profile: 
```
canary-3 | model=redwood-13b | kv_format=INT8 | batch=8
p50_decode_latency=34ms (was 38ms)
p99_decode_latency=162ms (was 148ms)
kv_mem=1.8GB (was 2.3GB)
throughput_tokens/s=1920 (was 1750)
eval_perplexity=+1.1 (baseline)
rouge_l=-2.4 on canonical QA prompts
```

Tess: interesting: latency and mem look good, but quality delta is non-trivial. small batches + int8 KV can increase quantization noise, especially if we used a short calibration corpus. did you calibrate with full-rep dataset?

Marta: no, quick 5k tokens from canary traces.

Harry: that could be the culprit. per-tensor cal on small shift-y data -> scaling mismatch. try per-channel or longer calib window. also check kernel selection: runtime might be switching some matmuls to FP8 vs INT8 and that heterogeneous mix can change numerical behavior.

Raj: I dug in. kernel-selector logs for the same run show: 
```
[ks] selected_kernel: kv_store=INT8_kv_fast
[ks] selected_kernel: matmul_proj=FP8_fast
[ks] hysteresis: enabled=true, hysteresis_ms=20
```
If matmul_proj is FP8 and kv is INT8, decode path has mixed-precision accumulation changes.

Marta: ok. what about batching heuristics? we saw smaller batches on canary because traffic spike -> more single-request batches which exacerbates quantization noise?

Tess: yes. batching reduces variance. small batches -> per-request activations have different dynamic ranges, quant scales on KV get less representative. in practice we observed RNG-like decode differences for specific prompts.

ci-bot: automated-repro run started (job=kv-int8-canary-repro, commit=abc123). will post results in ~5m.

Raj: short-term mitigation idea: add a kernel-selector preference for "quality-first" when model flagged as sensitive. fallback to FP8/FP16 for projection kernels if eval delta > threshold. we have a flag: `--kernel-pref=quality` but it's off by default.

Marta: can we test flipping `--kernel-pref=quality` on canary-3 and re-eval?

Harry: also try redoing calibration with per-channel sym quant and include more warmup traces: `calibrate_kv --mode per-channel --tokens 200k`. that usually stabilizes scales.

Tess: note: doing per-channel increases storage slightly (~+5%) but still < INT8 baseline. tradeoff seems worth it if rouge/perp improves.

ci-bot: repro finished. results: 
```
job=kv-int8-canary-repro | baseline=fp32-kv
int8_kv_shortcalib: rouge_l=-2.3 perp=+1.05 p99_lat=160ms
int8_kv_perchannel_200k: rouge_l=-0.3 perp=+0.12 p99_lat=165ms
int8_kv_perchannel_200k + kernel-pref=quality: rouge_l=+0.0 perp=-0.02 p99_lat=170ms
```

Marta: looks like per-channel calib recovers most quality but adds a bit of latency. kernel-pref=quality bumped p99 by ~5ms but fixed quality.

Raj: plan: 1) roll per-channel calib for canary-3 (Marta) 2) add run-time kernel-pref toggle and a hysteresis window so selector doesn't flip too often (Raj) 3) run larger smoke eval (Tess) 4) update release notes w/ perf/quality tradeoffs (Harry)

Marta: assigning: I'll run `calibrate_kv --mode per-channel --tokens 200k` and push a canary build with that calibration file by EOD.

Raj: I'll prototype kernel-pref and increase hysteresis_ms to 50ms in selector config, then open PR with tests.

Tess: I'll run the 1k prompt eval and post detailed diffs; will include per-prompt failure cases so we can decide if certain prompt patterns are more sensitive (e.g., long-code blocks, many dates).

Harry: add test matrix for batch sizes (1,2,8,32) in CI for quantized KV variants. we should catch small-batch sensitivity before rollout.

ops-bot: Deploy monitor: canary-3 traffic is at 12% and rollback window set to 30m.

Marta: thanks. if per-channel still bad we'll revert to FP8-KV or keep fp32 for KV and quantize only weights. will update when canary results land. :thumbsup:

Raj: also logging note: add `quant_scale_mean` and `quant_scale_std` to per-request traces so we can monitor drift in production quickly.

Tess: good call. that'll help detect calibration drift over time.

Marta: closing loop once we have CI matrix and canary re-run. cheers.
